art.why: No NGA painting of the four virtues personified in the open data (searched prudence, justice, temperance, fortitude, virtue, allegory). Lotto's Allegory of Virtue and Vice is claimed by plato.

art.title: Study for a Ceiling with the Personification of Counsel
art.why: No Prudence in the collection; Counsel (good deliberation) is the part of prudence Aquinas treats first. The gallery's description sees only a cherub with a wreath-like object among clouds and figures below: the look text must say no more than that, and name the subject only from the title.
No Justice with scales, Judgement of Solomon or Justice of Trajan in the open data.

art.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Bartholomew
art.why: Aquinas's courage is endurance and the martyr its perfect form: the apostle bound to a post, looking up into the light. Raphael's St George is already used.

art.title: Allegory
art.why: A winged woman holding the reins of a rearing horse: desire held, not killed. The gallery's description does not name the virtue, so the look text must not call her Temperance; say the picture is usually read as passion governed and flag it.
No NGA painting of the virtues together.

music.why: O virtus Sapientiae: the power of Wisdom, the virtue Wisdom of Solomon 8:7 says teaches the other four. Also proposed for right-and-wrong s2: use in one only.
A hymn of the martyrs who 'fought the good fight': courage as endurance.
Grace, not achievement: the Lutheran side of the objection in one hymn.
